glossEn: Are you coming with us tonight?
notes: Marker: tú-form 2sg vienes (the T verb agreement; the pronoun is dropped).

glossEn: What are you doing this weekend?

notes: Marker: tú-imperative Llámame plus tú-subjunctive llegues.

glossEn: Hey, will you lend me your bike?
notes: Marker: tú-imperative Oye, tú-form prestas, and T-possessive tu.
Marker: V-pronoun usted with 3sg conditional podría; V-form maps to polite.
Marker: usted-form 3sg desea addressed to the hearer, confirmed by the vocative señora.

text: Buenos días, señor García. ¿Cómo está usted?
glossEn: Good morning, Mr. García. How are you?
notes: Marker: title-plus-surname address señor García with V-pronoun usted.
Marker: usted-imperative Pase (3sg subjunctive form) with explicit usted.
Trap: por favor is a fossilized courtesy formula and sets no register; the tú-imperative pásame fixes the sentence as casual.

glossEn: Thanks so much! You're a sweetheart.
notes: Trap: gracias is a fossilized formula; the tú-form eres fixes the sentence as casual.

glossEn: Can you tell him from me: 'call me tomorrow'?
notes: Trap: the quoted tú-imperative llámame is casual, but the frame's usted-form puede addresses the hearer politely; the frame's register governs.

text: El tren a Sevilla sale a las ocho.
glossEn: The train to Seville leaves at eight.
notes: Third-person statement with no addressee and no T/V form.

text: En agosto hace mucho calor en Madrid.
glossEn: In August it is very hot in Madrid.
